21: ## Overview
22: 
23: Dune: Imperium – Uprising is a deck-building worker placement game set in the Dune universe. Each player is a Leader representing one of the Great Houses of the Landsraad (or another powerful figure). You play cards to send Agents to board spaces, acquire new cards for your deck, deploy units (troops and sandworms) to the Conflict, and grow Influence with the four Factions (Emperor, Spacing Guild, Bene Gesserit, Fremen). At the end of a round, if any player has reached **10 or more Victory Points** (or the Conflict Deck is empty), the game ends and whoever has the most VP wins.
24: 
25: Compared with base Dune: Imperium, the rulebook's difference notes call out: Spies and observation posts, a new **Spy** Agent icon, additional board spaces requiring 2 Influence with a Faction, sandworms and Maker Hooks, Battle Icons and Sandworm Reward Doubling, Objective cards (which determine the first player), and the new optional CHOAM Module. There is **no Mentat** Agent and there are **no Foldspace** cards. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
26: 
27: **Scope:** Original English 2023 Uprising, rulebook version 23-10-12: complete standard 2–4-player play, including the required two-player Rival rules below, plus the optional standard base-box CHOAM Module. Solo-only rules, all optional Rival variants (including Streamlined Rivals), six-player teams and cross-game expansions are excluded. In two-player play use an ordinary scoring Rival, rather than the two Streamlined-only Rivals Lady Amber Metulli and Glossu “The Beast” Rabban. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are identified for sorting only and are not used in this scope. Shaddam’s printed setup instruction is verified against the original Leader card reproduced in the publisher’s October 4, 2023 Contracts design diary. Board-space rules come from the publisher’s Uprising Board Space Guide; the labeled FAQ section uses relevant clarifications from the official January 13, 2025 FAQ.

97: ## Turn Structure
98: 
99: A game is played in a series of rounds, each with five phases in this order:
100: 
101: ### Phase 1: Round Start
102: Reveal a new Conflict card from the top of the Conflict Deck and place it face up next to the deck (on top of any Conflict cards remaining from previous rounds). Resolve any defensive troop bonus for a location already controlled when its Conflict is revealed: its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict, without an Agent visit. Then each player draws **five** cards from their own deck to form their hand.
103: 
104: ### Phase 2: Player Turns
105: Starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise, players take one turn at a time: either an **Agent turn** or a **Reveal turn**. Generally you take Agent turns until you run out of Agents, then a Reveal turn — but Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents. Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase. In standard 3–4-player play, the phase ends when all players have taken a Reveal turn. In two-player play, skip the humans who have Revealed but continue the Rival’s Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply; proceed to Combat only once both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never Reveals. You may play **Plot Intrigue** cards at any point during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns. Pay an entry cost using resources you already hold at that moment. On an Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing your Agent; resources it grants before entry join your available supply and can also pay that cost. Gains that occur only after placement, from the destination or played Agent card, cannot pay for that same entry.
106: 
107: **Card anatomy:** each deck card has an Agent box and a Reveal box; on a given turn you use only one of them (Agent box on an Agent turn, Reveal box on a Reveal turn). Cards may also show a Faction (not all do), Agent icons, a Persuasion cost (top right), and sometimes an Acquire effect.
108: 
109: **Agent Turn:** Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and use it to send an Agent from your Leader to an **unoccupied** board space whose upper-left icon matches one of the card's Agent icons (Spies provide an alternative — see Special Rules). You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents. A connected Spy alone does not give every card Spy-Agent access: you need a matching normal Agent icon on the played card, or its **Spy Agent icon** with your Spy at a connected post. Infiltrate bypasses another player’s occupancy, not the card-icon requirement. You can't send an Agent to a space that already has one (Spies can provide a way around this). You must pay any costs and meet any requirements of the space — if you can't pay the cost immediately (before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played), you can't send your Agent there. Then gain the effects of the board space and of the card's **Agent box** (ignore its Reveal box); if the space belongs to a Faction, also advance your cube one space on that Faction's Influence track. You may carry out all these effects in any order. A card with no Agent icons can't be played on an Agent turn — it may only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
110: 
111: **Reveal Turn:** Three steps in order:
112: - **Reveal Cards:** Reveal all cards remaining in your hand, placing them face up in front of you, kept separate from cards played on Agent turns.
113: - **Resolve Reveal Effects:** Gain the **Reveal box** effects of the just-revealed cards only (not of cards played on Agent turns), in any order. You may use gained **Persuasion** to acquire cards before, between, or after your Reveal effects. Total your Combat **strength**, announce it, and set your Combat marker at any point while resolving, updating it as needed (this timing lets cards like the Gurney Halleck Leader reference your strength during your Reveal turn).
114: - **Clean Up:** Move all cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.
115: 
116: ### Phase 3: Combat
117: First, Combat Intrigue: starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise, each player with **at least one unit in the Conflict** may play any number of **Combat Intrigue** cards, or pass. Once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively, resolve the Combat using the adjusted strength shown on the track.

172: ## Special Rules & Edge Cases
173: 
174: - **Spies & observation posts:** Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional: you may decline even if a legal placement or recall exists. The **Spy icon** (on a card or board space) lets you place a Spy from your supply on an **unoccupied** observation post; if you have no Spies in your supply when you need to place one, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. Some placement effects (e.g., from the Lady Margot Fenring Leader) specify a particular Agent icon that must be connected to the post — otherwise you can't place the Spy.
